notes.W7236862650: A subzone of Wernicke's area (left posterior STG) fires before speech, is causally needed for it, and encodes whole upcoming words. That resolves why 'comprehension' lesions wreck production, and its signals already decode intended speech in paralysis. Small invasive cohort.
notes.W7110625727: An 80-minute aspirations workshop, cross-randomised with large cash transfers across 415 Kenyan villages, raised labour, investment and living standards 17 months later. Cash also raised aspirations, suggesting a psychological channel inside economic aid. Mechanism attribution is the softer claim.
notes.W7154454518: With ~783,000 memory tests from ~219,000 people, later-born cohorts both start old age sharper and decline more slowly. The size of the gap could account for the 13% per-decade fall in dementia incidence. Cohort comparisons remain observational despite a bounding analysis.
notes.W7225627285: A 40-week RCT in 120 adults: adding thrice-weekly resistance training to tirzepatide left weight loss unchanged but saved about 1.1 kg of lean mass and turned strength losses into gains. A practical answer to the muscle worry about incretins; modest sample, short horizon.
notes.W7159704871: Tethered moths under a randomised star field held their migratory heading on magnetic cues alone. Inverting inclination reversed them; removing violet–blue light or adding weak RF noise abolished it. Classic radical-pair signatures, now shown in a long-distance insect migrant.
notes.W7118799519: Proves the Berry–Tabor prediction of Poisson pair statistics for a particle in a 3D box with Diophantine side ratios, via Ratner's theorem on unipotent orbits. A rare rigorous foothold for quantum chaos's integrable side; covers the two-point density only.
notes.W4410991547: Using unsealed court evidence of labour-market collusion, firms that start sharing executives or directors become 11 percentage points more likely to collude, a ninefold rise. Directly relevant to dormant Clayton Act Section 8 enforcement; evidence is from detected cases only.
notes.W7213258944: A quantum-gas microscope for fermionic strontium-87 reads out all ten nuclear-spin states atom by atom in one shot. That opens site-resolved study of SU(N) magnetism, which spin-1/2 lattices cannot reach. Many-body correlations are so far shown in simulation, not measured.
notes.W4407884439: Thousands of reaching trials over weeks, instead of a few hundred, reveal near-complete adaptation, growing retention and spontaneous recovery, and narrowing generalisation. Standard lab-timescale models of motor learning may describe only the opening act. Samples of 10 and 18.
notes.W7128466625: A 1.29-gram flapping-wing robot hovers and tracks trajectories with only onboard sensors and computation, leaving the motion-capture room for the first time in its class. A 30-second flight dodged obstacles and landed on a sunflower; still tethered for power and human-steered.

thread: Two of today's picks treat supposedly fixed human capacities as movable. In Kenya, a short workshop and cash both shifted aspirations, and with them investment. Across Western cohorts, later generations reach old age with better memory and slower decline. In both, the target is a trajectory set early by environment and expectation, not a fixed endowment, which changes where interventions should aim.

notes.W7236305771: Shifts: interstitial atoms like oxygen in metals sit randomly → in α-titanium they occupy correlated columns forming hidden ordered nanodomains. Models of strengthening, diffusion and phase stability built on random interstitials need a correlated-defect starting point.
notes.W7160248457: Shifts: efficient tiling and long-range order in tissues are separate properties needing separate control → one local growth-plus-repulsion rule produces both, driving microglia toward hyperuniformity. Tissue patterning can achieve global order without global regulation.
notes.W4411174673: Shifts: regulatory architectures are explained by detailed molecular mechanism → selection on the genotype-phenotype map itself yields a maximisation principle and 'frequency matching'. Parameters of gene regulation become predictable from population genetics, and evolvability gains a testable definition.
notes.W4403797072: Shifts: universality limits for orthogonal polynomials are proved case by case → sine-kernel and other limits hold exactly when the spectral measure has a unique suitable tangent measure. Universality classes become a local geometric property of the measure.

foundation.title: Brains learn by building predictive internal models
foundation.principle: Behaviour is driven by internal models that predict sensory consequences before they arrive, and learning is the slow refinement of those models. The Wernicke's-area subzone that encodes whole words before they are spoken is a case: a region labelled 'perceptual' turns out to generate the expected percept that speech must match, which is why its damage breaks production. The weeks-long reaching study is another: with extended practice the motor memory nears full compensation and its generalisation narrows, as an internal model tunes itself to the specific dynamics it predicts. The same logic underlies predictive coding in vision, efference copy in electric fish and crickets, and model-based control in robotics, including insect-scale fliers that must estimate their own state onboard.
rests_on: Wolpert, Ghahramani & Jordan (1995). An internal model for sensorimotor integration
Friston (2010). The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory?
foundation.question: Are perception and production served by one shared predictive model, or by separate models that learn to stay in register?

W7236862650.question: Why does damage to Wernicke's area, a comprehension region, also disrupt speech production?
W7236862650.approach: Direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation and lesion analysis around the posterior superior temporal gyrus.
W7236862650.finding: Left posterior STG activates before speech, is causally necessary for production, and encodes whole upcoming words, not acoustics.
W7236862650.implication: Wernicke's area contains a generative speech subregion; a new target for speech neuroprostheses in paralysis.

W7110625727.question: Do higher aspirations drive long-term investment by people in poverty, and do aspirations respond to income?
W7110625727.approach: 415-village field experiment, 8,300 Kenyan women; aspirations workshop cross-randomised with large unconditional cash transfers.
W7110625727.finding: Workshop raised aspirations, labour supply, investment, revenue and living standards at 17 months; cash transfers also raised aspirations.
W7110625727.implication: Cheap psychological interventions can complement cash in development policy; aspirations are a lever, not a fixed trait.

W7154454518.question: Is falling dementia incidence due to higher cognition entering old age, slower decline, or both?
W7154454518.approach: ~783,000 episodic memory assessments from ~219,000 people in five longitudinal cohorts, compared by birth cohort.
W7154454518.finding: Later cohorts start higher and decline slower; the 20-year cohort advantage could explain the 13% per-decade incidence fall.
W7154454518.implication: Lifespan environmental conditions reshape cognitive ageing itself, supporting prevention beyond late-life treatment.

W7225627285.question: Can resistance exercise limit lean mass loss during tirzepatide weight loss?
W7225627285.approach: Two-arm RCT, 120 adults on tirzepatide, thrice-weekly resistance training vs usual activity for 40 weeks.
W7225627285.finding: Weight loss similar (~22 kg); lean loss 3.57 vs 4.67 kg (difference 1.09 kg); strength rose with training, fell without.
W7225627285.implication: Resistance training is an effective adjunct to incretin therapy, preserving muscle and function.

W7159704871.question: What kind of magnetic compass lets Bogong moths navigate when stars are hidden?
W7159704871.approach: Tethered flight arena under randomised star sky with manipulated magnetic field, light spectrum and radiofrequency noise.
W7159704871.finding: Moths orient by inclination; inverting inclination reverses flight; removing 380–500 nm light or weak RF abolishes orientation.
W7159704871.implication: Bogong moths use a light-dependent, radical-pair-based inclination compass for long-distance night migration.

W7118799519.question: Do energy levels of a quantum particle in a 3D box follow Poisson pair statistics, as Berry–Tabor predicted?
W7118799519.approach: Recast the counting as theta-function averages over unipotent orbits on SL(2,Z)³\SL(2,R)³; apply Ratner's theorem.
W7118799519.finding: Two-point spectral density is Poisson for boxes with Diophantine side ratios, e.g. 1, 2^(1/3), 2^(-1/3), with convergence rate.
W7118799519.implication: Extends Eskin–Margulis–Mozes from 2D to 3D, advancing rigorous quantum chaos via homogeneous dynamics.

W4410991547.question: Does sharing executives or board directors make firms more likely to collude?
W4410991547.approach: Explicit labour-market collusion measure from unsealed court evidence, comparing firm pairs before and after common leadership.
W4410991547.finding: Collusion probability rises 11 percentage points after common leadership begins, ninefold over baseline; not explained by competition closeness.
W4410991547.implication: Supports stronger enforcement of Clayton Act Section 8 against interlocking directorates.

W7213258944.question: Can single atoms in SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard systems be imaged with full spin resolution?
W7213258944.approach: Quantum-gas microscope for fermionic 87Sr using 689 nm narrow-line cooling and fluorescence plus spin-selective optical pumping.
W7213258944.finding: Occupation of all ten spin states read in one realisation; Larmor precession tracked across the spin-9/2 manifold.
W7213258944.implication: Enables site-resolved study of exotic SU(N) magnetism and new detection for quantum simulation and metrology.

W4407884439.question: How does a motor memory develop over thousands of trials and weeks, rather than one session?
W4407884439.approach: Force-field reaching adaptation over nine sessions (n = 10 and 18), testing retention, transfer, decay, recovery, generalisation.
W4407884439.finding: Near-complete compensation, long-term gains in retention and spontaneous recovery, and narrowing angular generalisation.
W4407884439.implication: Short-session studies miss major changes; rehabilitation and training models need long-timescale data.

W7128466625.question: Can an insect-scale flapping-wing robot fly stably with only onboard sensing and computation?
W7128466625.approach: 1.29 g robot with IMU, optical flow and time-of-flight sensors, onboard estimators, low-level and hierarchical control.
W7128466625.finding: Centimetre-scale positional accuracy; a 30 s free flight avoided obstacles and landed on a sunflower.
W7128466625.implication: Moves microrobots beyond motion-capture arenas toward field tasks; onboard planning and power are next.

figure_notes.W7154454518: Each line traces episodic memory for one birth cohort across the ages it was observed. Because cohorts overlap in age, compare lines at the same age: later-born cohorts sit higher (better memory) and slope less steeply downward (slower decline). That vertical gap plus flatter slope is the 'double dividend'.
figure_notes.W7225627285: This is the trial's CONSORT diagram: read top to bottom to see how 1,251 screened people narrowed to the randomised participants, and how many in each arm completed 40 weeks. It shows the trial's funnel and dropout, which matters for judging whether the lean-mass result is robust.
figure_notes.W7159704871: Panel a shows the moth itself; panel b maps probable spring migration routes from breeding grounds to the Australian Alps, with the non-magnetic test lab marked in green; panel c shows the cave walls where around 17,000 moths per square metre aestivate. It sets the navigational problem the experiments address.
figure_notes.W7213258944: Panel a is the hardware: atoms in an optical lattice inside a glass cell, a vertical magnetic field, a horizontal 689 nm imaging beam and a high-aperture objective collecting fluorescence. Panel b sketches the SU(10) Hubbard model, where only one spin state is imaged at a time; panel c gives the level scheme behind that selectivity.
figure_notes.W4407884439: Panel a plots reaching error across nine training sessions: errors start large when the force field switches on and shrink towards zero over weeks. Panel b summarises error at the end of each session versus baseline, with letters marking statistically distinct sessions, showing adaptation still improving long after a typical one-day study would stop.
figure_notes.W7128466625: A shows the robot landing on a sunflower; B–E show the bare robot, its three sensor and compute boards, and the integrated 1.29 g vehicle from above and below. F compares lift: the scaled-up module gives 46% more than an earlier design. G is a composite of a free flight weaving around obstacles.
